title: All About Me: Settling & Attachment Basket
strapline: A photo of home, a comforter that smells of Mum, a family voice on the tablet — the little basket that holds a baby steady.
intent: Ease settling and separation by keeping precious pieces of home close — familiar faces, scents, sounds and comforters within reach.
Strengthen the bond between baby and key person and the sense that this new place holds their people too.
Support a baby's emerging sense of self — their own name, their own face, their own family — during the big transition into nursery.
Offer real comfort at the hard moments of the day: arrival, sleep, a wobble in the afternoon.
Build the trust and security that let a baby, in time, turn from the basket to the wider room and explore.
implementation: Make a personal basket with each family: laminated family photos, a comforter or muslin that smells of home, a recorded lullaby or voice message, a familiar small object.
Keep it always accessible so a baby can reach for their people whenever they need to, not only at set times.
Use it at the tender moments — offer the family photo at drop-off, the comforter at sleep, the recorded voice in an afternoon dip.
Talk warmly about the family with the baby ('there's Mummy — she's coming back after your sleep'), naming and holding them close.
Refresh photos and voices as families change, respect what is precious, and store comforters safely between uses.
key_questions: Shall we find your photo of home?
Here's the blanket that smells like Mummy — does that feel better?
Would you like to hear Daddy's voice?
Who is this in your picture — is that your big brother?
Mummy's coming back after sleep — shall we keep her photo close?

impact.text: A baby reaches for their comforter and family photo and is soothed, the bond with home and key person holding them steady.
Studying their own photo and hearing their own name, a baby's sense of self grows — this is me, these are mine.
With familiar faces and scents close, a baby separates and settles into the day with the support of a familiar adult.
A baby turns to their own name and to the familiar voices and words the basket brings from home.

enhancements: Laminated family photos on a ring, small enough to hold and carry.
A recorded lullaby or family voice message on a simple sound button.
A comforter or muslin brought from home, kept for that baby alone.
A soft family photo book the baby can turn the pages of themselves.
A key-person photo too, so the trusted nursery face is part of the basket.

playing_exploring: The baby explores their own basket freely — turning photos, holding the comforter, pressing the voice button.
Familiar faces, scents and sounds invite calm, self-chosen comfort.
active_learning: A baby learns that their people can be found and held close here, and grows steadier for knowing it.
creating_thinking: A baby begins to hold their family in mind even when apart, comforted by photo and voice until they return.
